data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) defines the requirements for the management and use of Emergency Communications Systems within the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).
policy_statements.target: requirements for the management and use of Emergency Communications Systems within the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA)

policy_statements.source_text: This policy ensures that USDA’s emergency responders and key officials can continue to communicate in the event of natural disasters, acts of terrorism, and man-made disasters by maintaining interoperable emergency communication systems.
policy_statements.target: USDA’s emergency responders and key officials

policy_statements.source_text: USDA will leverage Federally-managed enterprise capabilities to assist in meeting emergency communications.

This DR applies to all USDA Federal employees, and any category of non-Federal person who performs duties in partnership with or on behalf of USDA, such as a consultant, contractor, advisor, volunteer, student, or intern.
policy_statements.target: all USDA Federal employees, and any category of non-Federal person who performs duties in partnership with or on behalf of USDA, such as a consultant, contractor, advisor, volunteer, student, or intern

policy_statements.source_text: This policy applies to all communications systems used to support critical functions performed by the Department.
policy_statements.target: all communications systems used to support critical functions performed by the Department

policy_statements.source_text: This policy supersedes DR 3300-001-J, National Security and Emergency Preparedness Telecommunications, dated March 23, 1999, in its entirety.
cross_references: DR 3300-001-J, National Security and Emergency Preparedness Telecommunications, dated March 23, 1999

policy_statements.source_text: This policy is effective immediately when published and will remain in effect until it is superseded or expires.
conditions: immediately when published
until it is superseded or expires

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA agencies will align processes, procedures, and any applicable policies with this DR within 6 months of the publication date, reviewing and updating them as needed annually thereafter.
policy_statements.target: processes, procedures, and any applicable policies
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices that are in an agreement or contract that goes beyond 6 months may request a waiver from the Director, Office of Homeland Security (OHS) to delay compliance until the existing agreement ends.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: that are in an agreement or contract that goes beyond 6 months
until the existing agreement ends

policy_statements.source_text: The OHS is the primary office within USDA assigned to manage access to Interagency Enterprise Level Emergency Communications Programs.
policy_statements.target: Interagency Enterprise Level Emergency Communications Programs

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices that need access to emergency communications platforms and/or services must request support through the OHS National Security Systems Program (NSSP).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: that need access to emergency communications platforms and/or services

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will utilize Federal partner or Departmental Enterprise Emergency Communications Systems prior to subscribing to or developing another service.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: Federal partner or Departmental Enterprise Emergency Communications Systems
conditions: prior to subscribing to or developing another service

policy_statements.source_text: Approval by the Chief Security Director, Office of Safety, Security and Protection (OSSP) and the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO), Office of the Chief Information Office (OCIO) is required prior to the acquisition of any new system.
conditions: prior to the acquisition of any new system

policy_statements.source_text: Personnel who support essential activities, emergency response, and continuity operations will be provided Government Emergency Telecommunications Service (GETS), Wireless Priority Service (WPS), and/or FirstNet service as required to complete their assigned duties.
policy_statements.target: Personnel who support essential activities, emergency response, and continuity operations
conditions: who support essential activities, emergency response, and continuity operations
as required to complete their assigned duties

policy_statements.source_text: Personnel provided emergency communications devices or capabilities must participate in routine and emergency testing of services.
policy_statements.actor_name: Personnel provided emergency communications devices or capabilities
policy_statements.target: routine and emergency testing of services
conditions: provided emergency communications devices or capabilities

policy_statements.source_text: Failure to comply with testing programs for two or more consecutive testing periods may result in cancellation of services.
conditions: Failure to comply with testing programs for two or more consecutive testing periods

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices who operate communications systems utilized for essential activities or emergency response must order Telecommunications Service Priority (TSP) for critical circuits supporting the system.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: who operate communications systems utilized for essential activities or emergency response
for critical circuits supporting the system

policy_statements.source_text: Departmental level continuity facilities will employ all required communications capabilities prescribed in accordance with White House Office of Science and Technology (OSTP)/Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Directive 16-1, Minimum Communications Requirements for Federal Executive Branch Continuity Communications Capabilities (OSTP/OMB D 16-1) and participate in all required interagency testing programs.
cross_references: White House Office of Science and Technology (OSTP)/Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Directive 16-1, Minimum Communications Requirements for Federal Executive Branch Continuity Communications Capabilities (OSTP/OMB D 16-1)

policy_statements.source_text: The alternate and devolution sites for Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must have, at a minimum, the following capabilities:
Satellite telephone with a fixed external antenna;
policy_statements.actor_name: alternate and devolution sites for Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Fax machine, utilizing an analog telephone line;
policy_statements.actor_name: alternate and devolution sites for Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Secure telephone, keyed at the appropriate classification level to support their operations and reporting status, but minimally keyed for unclassified communications;
policy_statements.actor_name: alternate and devolution sites for Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Alternate power supply/generator that provides backup power for critical facility infrastructure (lights, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning) and communication systems; and;
policy_statements.actor_name: alternate and devolution sites for Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Active TSP codes assigned for all mission critical data and voice communication circuits.
policy_statements.actor_name: alternate and devolution sites for Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: OHS is the primary office within USDA assigned to manage access to interagency enterprise level emergency communications programs.
policy_statements.target: interagency enterprise level emergency communications programs

policy_statements.source_text: TSP is available on telecommunications circuits used to support any Primary Mission Essential Function (PMEF), Mission Essential Function (MEF), Essential Supporting Activity (ESA), and other functions that have been determined critical to USDA’s ability to effectively perform its mission;
conditions: that have been determined critical to USDA’s ability to effectively perform its mission

policy_statements.source_text: GETS and WPS services are available for personnel who support USDA critical and emergency functions who require priority services during periods with degraded or saturated telecommunications services;
conditions: who support USDA critical and emergency functions who require priority services during periods with degraded or saturated telecommunications services

policy_statements.source_text: FirstNet communications are employed as appropriate to assist first responders, key Departmental continuity personnel, and others supporting critical and emergency functions; and

Shared Resources (SHARES) High Frequency (HF) Radio Program, is a communications system that supports national security and emergency preparedness operations when traditional landline and cellular communications are unavailable.
conditions: when traditional landline and cellular communications are unavailable
policy_statements.actor_name: Shared Resources (SHARES) High Frequency (HF) Radio Program

policy_statements.source_text: OSSP is the primary office within USDA assigned to manage Departmental Enterprise Level Emergency Notification Systems.
policy_statements.target: Departmental Enterprise Level Emergency Notification Systems

policy_statements.source_text: One or more Emergency Notification systems processes are available to provide urgent notifications to Departmental personnel at the USDA Headquarters level in the National Capital Region.
Regional and local field offices are encouraged to leverage the enterprise system or utilize a comparable process/system to ensure that all staff can receive urgent notifications for their area.
OHS and OCIO are responsible for ensuring that the minimum continuity communications requirements for Federal Executive Departments and Agencies outlined in OSTP/OMB D 16-1 are met.
policy_statements.target: minimum continuity communications requirements for Federal Executive Departments and Agencies outlined in OSTP/OMB D 16-1

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of OHS will:
Ensure that emergency communication guidance is available to Departmental Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices;
Coordinate with OCIO and OSSP to provide a Departmental Enterprise Emergency Notification System; and
Provide guidance, direction, and oversight for USDA’s participation with Federal partner-provided emergency communications systems and services.
policy_statements.target: USDA’s participation with Federal partner-provided emergency communications systems and services

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CIO will:
Assist OHS with the management and validation of communication circuits enrolled in the TSP program;
Coordinate with OHS on enterprise level communications support contracts to ensure that emergency support capabilities are evaluated;
Assist the OHS with the operation, maintenance, and testing of all of the Department’s primary alternate location and devolution site’s Memorandum of Understanding; and
Coordinate with system owners to ensure that the communication systems approved to operate within the Department have adequate disaster recovery plans
Ensure Departmental communications portfolio management implementation of all emergency communications systems;
policy_statements.target: Departmental communications portfolio management implementation of all emergency communications systems

policy_statements.source_text: Assist Mission Area Assistant CIOs and agency site support personnel with implementation of emergency communication requirements.
policy_statements.target: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and agency site support personnel

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of OSSP will:
Serve as the Office of Primary Responsibility for the Departmental enterprise level Emergency Notification System;
policy_statements.target: Departmental enterprise level Emergency Notification System

policy_statements.source_text: Manage the selection and implementation of a Departmental Emergency Notification System;
policy_statements.target: selection and implementation of a Departmental Emergency Notification System

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with the OCIO to determine an appropriate information technology infrastructure that provides an acceptable level of resiliency for the Departmental Emergency Notification System; and
Coordinate with agencies and staff office to ensure that they have the capability to develop and implement procedures to meet their respective notification requirements.
The OHS NSSP Manager will:
Manage USDA’s GETS/WPS Program;
Serve as the USDA office approving, denying, and managing subscriptions;
Train USDA personnel on the GETS/WPS program, including official use policy;
Represent USDA at interagency meetings/discussions; and
Track the USDA official’s conduct of quarterly GETS/WPS testing.
policy_statements.target: USDA official’s conduct of quarterly GETS/WPS testing

policy_statements.source_text: Manage USDA’s TSP Program;
Serve as the focal point for managing TSP codes;
Advise Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officers of TSP code assignment by DHS; and
Coordinate with validation with DHS for TSP code validations assignments accordance with OSTP/OMB D 16-1.
Serve as the Agency Point of Contact (POC) for the FirstNet Program;
Define personnel eligibility requirements for the following two service categories:
Primary Users
Sworn law enforcement officials.
Fire fighting officials.
Departmental level continuity officials.
Support Users
Public health officials.
Select agency and staff office continuity officials.
Designated on-call personnel that support “Primary Users” when activated.
conditions: that support “Primary Users” when activated

policy_statements.source_text: Other personnel and/or devices that support USDAs critical response efforts during an emergency.
conditions: that support USDAs critical response efforts during an emergency

policy_statements.source_text: Manage the process to elevate “Support Users” to “Primary Users” when operations dictate.
conditions: when operations dictate

policy_statements.source_text: Establish procedures to request support from the FirstNet service provider for service.
policy_statements.target: procedures to request support from the FirstNet service provider for service

policy_statements.source_text: Process should include instructions for both preplanned events and emergency events that require additional communication support.
policy_statements.target: instructions for both preplanned events and emergency events that require additional communication support

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with OCIO, users, and application providers to ensure that applications used on FirstNet have an authority to operate and an assigned application manager if required.
conditions: if required

policy_statements.source_text: Note: Several applications have been developed, reviewed, and certified to operate on the FirstNet infrastructure.
Most of these applications are not FirstNet applications but are approved to operate on FirstNet devices.
Many of these applications have restrictions based on multiple factors as to who can access the application.
Users must request access to restricted applications from the application manager.
Coordinate with OCIO and the Procurement Operations Division to maintain a contract to procure FirstNet.
Manage USDA’s compliance with OSTP/OMB Directive 16-1;
Represent USDA at Continuity Communications Manager Group meetings;
Ensure that USDA maintains required systems and user proficiency;
Manage USDA’s compliance with Interagency Testing Programs;
policy_statements.target: USDA’s compliance with Interagency Testing Programs

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate testing for Departmental level continuity sites.
Respond to testing results.
Manage the receipt and internal handling and distribution of the interagency Continuity Communications Plan.
policy_statements.target: receipt and internal handling and distribution of the interagency Continuity Communications Plan

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Heads will:
Coordinate emergency communications needs with OHS;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Heads

policy_statements.source_text: Identify an appropriate number of POCs to manage their organization’s GETS/WPS subscriptions;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Heads

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with OHS to manage their TSP codes for telecommunications circuits requiring priority restoration services; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Heads
policy_statements.target: their TSP codes for telecommunications circuits requiring priority restoration services

policy_statements.source_text: Designate an appropriate number of POCs to manage their organization’s FirstNet subscriptions and any USDA developed application(s).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Heads

policy_statements.source_text: Authorized users will:
Order and cancel service for emergency communications as changes occur;
conditions: as changes occur

policy_statements.source_text: Report the loss, theft, or damage to any emergency communications equipment;
policy_statements.target: loss, theft, or damage to any emergency communications equipment

policy_statements.source_text: Participate in testing as requested; and
conditions: as requested

policy_statements.source_text: Utilize priority services only when operationally necessary, for training or testing purposes.
conditions: only when operationally necessary, for training or testing purposes

policy_statements.section_title: Penalties and Disciplinary Actions for Non-Compliance
policy_statements.source_text: DR 4070-735-001, Employee Responsibilities and Conduct, Section 16, sets forth the USDA’s policies, procedures, and standards on employee responsibilities and conduct relative to the use of computers and telecommunications equipment.
cross_references: DR 4070-735-001, Employee Responsibilities and Conduct, Section 16

policy_statements.section_title: Penalties and Disciplinary Actions for Non-Compliance
policy_statements.source_text: In addition, DR 4070-735-001, Section 21, Disciplinary or Adverse Action, states:
cross_references: DR 4070-735-001, Section 21, Disciplinary or Adverse Action

policy_statements.section_title: Penalties and Disciplinary Actions for Non-Compliance
policy_statements.source_text: A violation of any of the responsibilities and conduct standards contained in this directive may be cause for disciplinary or adverse action; and

policy_statements.section_title: Penalties and Disciplinary Actions for Non-Compliance
policy_statements.source_text: Disciplinary or adverse action will be effective in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are required to conform to this policy.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: However, in the event that a specific policy requirement cannot be met as explicitly stated, Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may submit a waiver request.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: in the event that a specific policy requirement cannot be met as explicitly stated

policy_statements.source_text: The waiver request must explain the reason for the request, identify compensating security controls and actions that meet the intent of the policy, and identify how the compensating controls and actions provide a similar or greater level of defense or compliance than the policy requirement.

Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will address all policy waiver request memoranda to the OHS Director and submit the request to <OHSEC-NSSP-SupportTeam@usda.gov> for review and determination.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: All questions regarding this DR should be directed to the USDA NSSP Support Team at <OHSEC-NSSP-SupportTeam@usda.gov>.

extract_result.purpose:
a. This Departmental Regulation (DR) defines the requirements for the management and use of Emergency Communications Systems within the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).
b. This policy ensures that USDA’s emergency responders and key officials can continue to communicate in the event of natural disasters, acts of terrorism, and man-made disasters by maintaining interoperable emergency communication systems. USDA will leverage Federally-managed enterprise capabilities to assist in meeting emergency communications.
extract_result.scope:
a. This DR applies to all USDA Federal employees, and any category of non-Federal person who performs duties in partnership with or on behalf of USDA, such as a consultant, contractor, advisor, volunteer, student, or intern.
b. This policy applies to all communications systems used to support critical functions performed by the Department.

This Departmental Regulation (DR) defines the requirements for the management and use of Emergency Communications Systems within the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).

Departmental Enterprise Level Emergency Notification Systems
One or more Emergency Notification systems processes are available to provide urgent notifications to Departmental personnel at the USDA Headquarters level in the National Capital Region.
Regional and local field offices are encouraged to leverage the enterprise system or utilize a comparable process/system to ensure that all staff can receive urgent notifications for their area.
